headline: Day after Palestine, Priyanka Gandhi’s handbag message expresses solidarity with Bangladesh minorities
description: "The government should raise the issue of atrocities against minorities, both Hindus and Christians, in Bangladesh. It should discuss this with the Bangladesh government and support those who are in pain," she had said.
content:
After turning heads on Monday with a handbag bearing the word “Palestine” in Parliament, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra shifted focus on Tuesday and expressed solidarity with minorities in Bangladesh. Vadra was seen carrying a cream-colored handbag with the message “Bangladesh ke Hindu aur Isaiyon ke saath khade ho” (Stand with the Hindus and Christians of Bangladesh).
She was joined by several Congress MPs, and together they staged a protest in the Parliament premises. The MPs, holding handbags emblazoned with the message “Stand with minorities of Bangladesh,” raised slogans and demanded justice.
On Monday, Vadra had sought the government’s support for those who are in pain because of the attacks in Bangladesh. “The government should raise the issue of atrocities against minorities, both Hindus and Christians, in Bangladesh. It should discuss this with the Bangladesh government and support those who are in pain,” she had said.
Earlier, Vadra had turned heads on Monday with another handbag bearing the word “Palestine,” showcasing her support for Palestinians amid the Gaza conflict. The symbolic gestures have sparked significant discussions in Parliament, highlighting her commitment to global humanitarian causes.
In June, Gandhi criticised Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for what she described as the Israeli government’s “genocidal actions” in Gaza, accusing him and his administration of “barbarism.” Her comments followed Netanyahu’s defense of Israel’s ongoing war in Gaza during a speech to the US Congress.

headline: ‘My father could not tolerate the uproar’: Son of official who died at BPSC exam centre in Patna amid ruckus
description: Bihar Public Service Commission orders re-exam at centre where 6,500 aspirants wrote Combined Competitive Examination prelims
content:
Three days after protests over an alleged delay in the distribution of question papers in a competitive exam led to chaos at an exam centre in Patna, the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) on Monday ordered a re-exam for those who took the test at the centre.
Amid the ruckus at the centre on Friday, an official on duty, additional centre superintendent Ram Iqbal Singh, suffered a heart attack and died.
Patna District Magistrate Chandrashekhar Singh told The Indian Express: “As additional centre superintendent Ram Iqbal Singh had to be rushed to hospital following a heart attack, students should have cooperated. Instead, they tried to block our way. The police have lodged cases against some students.”
According to an administration official, 58-year-old Ram Iqbal Singh was a teacher at Godani College in Arwal.

His son Sunny Kumar said the government should ensure that exams are held in an atmosphere where such incidents do not happen.
“My father had suffered a heart attack earlier as well. There had been so much tension and uproar at the centre, and my father could not tolerate it. He should have cited medical reasons to skip examination duty. The state government should ensure a congenial and tension-free atmosphere at examination centres so that such incidents do not take place in the future,” he said.
On Friday, more than 5 lakh students took the prelims of the Combined Competitive Examination (CCE), for filling vacancies in Group A and Group B posts, at 912 exam centres across Bihar.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
At the Bapu Pariksha Parisar in Kumhrar, Patna, some examinees took out a protest, alleging a delay in the distribution of question papers, following which the Patna administration rushed law enforcement forces to the centre.
During the protest, Iqbal Singh suffered a heart attack, and a woman examinee fainted.
BPSC chairman Tanvi Manubhai S Parmar on Monday told reporters: “We have decided to cancel the preliminary examination held at Bapu Pariksha Parisar examination centre due to ruckus caused by a group of unruly aspirants as part of a conspiracy to disrupt the exam.”
Around 6,500 aspirants who were allocated the Patna centre will now have to take the prelims again. The BPSC has not yet announced the date for the re-exam.

The commission said that 30-40 aspirants had been identified and that police were in the process of identifying more involved in the ruckus, the chairman said, adding that they would be debarred from appearing in the future, including in the rescheduled CCE prelims.

headline: Candidate gets 101.66 marks out of 100 in MP recruitment exam; job aspirants protest
description: The Madhya Pradesh Employees Selection Board clarified the "process of normalisation" has been adopted in the Van and Jail Recruitment Test 2023 as per rules, because of which candidates can get more than full marks (100) and less than zero.
content:
Job aspirants have staged a protest in Indore, raising questions over a candidate getting 101.66 marks out of the total 100 due to the adoption of “normalisation” process in a Madhya Pradesh government recruitment examination.
The protesters have alleged fraud in the recruitment examination and demanded a fair inquiry.
Normalisation is a process for ensuring students are neither advantaged nor disadvantaged by the difficulty of papers they write. The process involves revising the score of a student in a way that it becomes comparable with the score of another.
This becomes necessary when an examination of the same subject is held in multiple sessions, each with a different paper.
On Monday, some agitating unemployed youth gathered in front of the district collector’s office and handed over a memorandum addressed to Chief Minister Mohan Yadav to an officer, as per eyewitnesses.

The memorandum said that in the joint recruitment examination 2023 (Van and Jail Recruitment Test 2023) of forest and jail departments, a candidate scored 101.66 marks out of total 100 and topped the selection list.
The result of the examination, conducted by the Bhopal-headquartered Madhya Pradesh Employees Selection Board, was declared on December 13.
After the announcement of the result, the board clarified the “process of normalisation” has been adopted in the recruitment examination as per rules, because of which candidates can get more than full marks (100) and less than zero.

A leader of the protesters, Gopal Prajapat, told reporters, “This is the first time in the state’s history that a candidate has scored more than the total marks due to the normalisation process adopted in the recruitment exam. We are protesting against the unfair process of normalisation.” He alleged fraud in the recruitment exam held for the posts of forest guard, field guard (executive) and jail guard (executive), and demanded a fair inquiry.
Prajapat warned that if nothing is done in the matter, job aspirants will be forced to launch a bigger agitation

headline: Phone-tapping case: Ashok Gehlot’s former OSD turns approver
description: In an FIR lodged in Delhi in March 2021 based on the complaint of Union Minister and Rajasthan BJP leader Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Sharma and others were accused of criminal conspiracy and “unlawfully intercepting telegraphic signals (telephonic conversation)”.
content:
Lokesh Sharma, the former Officer on Special Duty (OSD) of former CM Ashok Gehlot, Monday turned approver in the 2020 phone tapping case before the Patiala House Court in New Delhi.
In an FIR lodged in Delhi in March 2021 based on the complaint of Union Minister and Rajasthan BJP leader Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Sharma and others were accused of criminal conspiracy and “unlawfully intercepting telegraphic signals (telephonic conversation)”.
These interceptions pertain to the 2020 leak of three audio clips purportedly involving one Gajendra Singh — alleged to be the Union Minister — a middleman, Sanjay Jain, and then Congress MLAs Bhanwarlal Sharma and Vishvendra Singh. In the tapes, they were purportedly heard planning to topple the Gehlot government in the state. The revelations subsequently led to then Deputy CM and Congress state president Sachin Pilot leading an unsuccessful rebellion of 19 MLAs.
An application was submitted by Sharma seeking a pardon in the said FIR. On Monday, the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) at Patiala House Court granted pardon to Sharma following a plea that he will provide a comprehensive and true disclosure of the facts related to the offence and other offenders, Sharma’s lawyers said.
The CJM also observed that Sharma’s statement is crucial in identifying other accused persons potentially involved in the criminal conspiracy.
Sharma was arrested by the Delhi Police last month but subsequently released on bail as he had secured an anticipatory bail the week before.

headline: Kerala Police commando’s ‘suicide’ triggers row in Wayanad
description: Victim was with a unit that conducted anti-insurgency operations in the state. According to Congress T Siddique, he killed himself over harassment from higher ups.
content:
A Kerala Police commando has allegedly committed suicide by shooting himself with his service pistol.
The victim was identified as Vineeth, 36, a commando with SOG, which conducts anti-terrorist and anti-Maoist operations in Kerala. Vineeth, a native of Vengappally in Wayanad district, was attached to Malabar Special Police camp at Areekode in Malappuram, where he shot himself Sunday night.
According to data from Kerala’s home department, as many as 138 police personnel from the state ended life from 2016 to last month in 2024.
Police sources said a case for unnatural death has been registered and that a probe is ongoing.

'Told Abhishek Bachchan he wasted six months of my life': Apoorva Lakhia

Congress MLA T Siddique alleged that the commando killed himself over harassment from his higher ups. Quoting WhatsApp chats of the deceased police commando, Siddique told the media in Wayanad’s Kalpetta that Vineeth had sought a leave because wife is pregnant but his higher ups refused to grant it.
“His suicide note has clearly indicated the names of senior officials responsible for his death. This should be treated as a murder, not suicide. Three times he had applied for leave, but higher ups did not grant it. Officials responsible for Vineeth’s death should not be allowed to continue in service,” Siddique said.
Meanwhile, a close relative said Vineeth had been under “mental trauma” after he failed to clear a physical fitness test as part of his training.

In the wake of the rising suicides in the police department, the state government had last year commissioned a detailed study by the research wing of its police academy to find the reasons behind such action.
